subject: OroHealth POC: evaluation readiness + decision ladder
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@orohealth.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@orohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: OroHealth POC: evaluation readiness + decision ladder

Thanks again for taking the call today — great conversation and clear signal that a short, focused POC will answer the main integration questions fast. Recap + proposed plan below so we have a single source of truth.

Key objectives (what success looks like for OroHealth during the 3-week POC):
- Latency: model inference p95 < 150ms for 512-token requests under representative peak load (see throughput below).
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec with burst to 350 rps for 30s.
- Cost: target operational cost <= $0.0008 per token (billing estimate attached).
- Quality: automatic classification accuracy >= 92% on your sample dataset; human-review pass rate >= 88% for edge cases.

Proposed scope:
1) Integration: redirect a sandbox stream of 1k requests/day (your sample) to Redwood hosted endpoint.
2) Workload capture: we will run a 24-hour performance capture to estimate real token distributions.
3) Evaluation: run automated quality tests against the 500 labeled examples you provided and a 150-case human review batch.
4) Ops: enable prefix caching, continuous batching policy, and recommended quantization profile for cost testing.

Owners & SLAs:
- Marcus Lin (AE) — primary cadence owner, commercial questions
- Ben Carter (CSM) — onboarding & runbook ownership
- Soojin Lee (Solutions Eng) — integration + perf tuning
- Monica Patel (Security lead) — SOC/compliance kickoff if procurement needs it

Deliverables by end of POC (3 weeks):
- Performance readout (latency/throughput graphs), cost estimate variant, and recommended production config.
- Quality report (automated metrics + human review summary).
- Decision ladder: 1) proceed to Dedicated trial; 2) extend sandbox for further tuning; 3) pause and re-evaluate scope.

Next steps (please confirm):
- OroHealth provides a small sample webhook/credentials and the labeled dataset by Tue 29 Jun.
- Redwood will schedule a 60-min integration kickoff Wed 30 Jun (Sooj in lead).
- Confirm procurement contact for any MSA/PO work.

Attachments: orohealth_poc_scope_v1.pdf (scope & timeline), redwood-poc-cost-estimate.xlsx

Thanks — happy to adjust objectives if the team wants different thresholds.

– Marcus
Marcus Lin | Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@orohealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@orohealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OroHealth POC: evaluation readiness + decision ladder

Marcus — thanks for the thorough recap. This looks actionable and matches what we talked about. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) Latency target — the 512-token p95 is fine; for our UI the p50 matters a lot too (target p50 < 60ms).
2) Quality metric — our labeled dataset is 600 items (not 500), with 3 priority intents that must be >= 95% accuracy. The rest can be >= 88%.
3) Timeline — procurement may want an MSA before we push any data; I looped in procurement@orohealth.com.

We'll deliver the dataset and creds by Tue evening. Can we confirm the kickoff window Wed 30 Jun 10:00–11:00 PT?

Also, can Soojin include a short checklist of the minimum headers / auth format they need? That will speed our infra team's work.

— Alex
Head of ML | OroHealth

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@orohealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

On Mon, Jun 28, 2027 at 09:12 AM Alex Novak <alex.novak@orohealth.com> wrote:
> Marcus — thanks for the thorough recap. This looks actionable and matches what we talked about. A few clarifications from my side: 

Thanks Alex — will do. Short checklist below — I'll also drop a runnable cURL template in the kickoff calendar invite.

Minimum envelope for sandbox calls:
- Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> header (we'll create per-POC keys and rotate after end)
- Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
- Body: {
    "prompt": "...",
    "max_tokens": 512,
    "stream": false
  }
- Optional: X-Client-Request-Id header for idempotency (helps our traces)

Perf notes I want to flag before the kickoff:
- For the throughput target (200 rps sustained), we recommend a warmup run of 10–15 minutes to populate prefix/KV caches.
- We'll validate p95 latency with and without prefix caching to show tradeoffs.

I'll be on the kickoff Wed 30 Jun 10:00 PT. Marcus — can you send the calendar invite and include the Drive link?

— Soojin

Subject: Re: OroHealth POC: evaluation readiness + decision ladder

Quick notes on instrumentation and acceptance checks (so the ops team has a checklist during the POC):
- We will provision an isolated sandbox key and a monitoring dashboard. Access: OroHealth will get read-only view for duration of POC.
- Acceptance check #1 (integrations): sample end-to-end request + trace confirmed in dashboard.
- Acceptance check #2 (performance): 24-hour capture with synthetic replay + 30-minute sustained 250rps spike test.
- Acceptance check #3 (quality): automated test pass rate on prioritized intents >= 95% and human review pass rate >= 88% on edge set.

If those checks are met, our recommendation in the readout will be to move to a 2-week Dedicated trial with provisioned capacity and SLA. If not, decision ladder item 2 is to extend the sandbox for a focused 1-week tuning sprint.

Also attached is an export-friendly table I will fill during testing: redwood-poc-cost-estimate.xlsx (labels: scenario | p50/p95 | tokens/day | est $/token).

— Ben
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
